# E24 build plan

This is a reviewable implementation plan, not a greenlight or evidence of passing runtime gates. The design stays frozen. Two coders own disjoint concerns: one owns the safety core and its HTTP acceptance, the other owns warning presentation and browser acceptance. Keeping the safety core with one coder follows AGENTS.md:191. Both briefs include the binding corrections below.

## Build order

| Task | Builds | Dependency |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Deterministic warning core, configuration, persistence, ports, HTTP boundary and real HTTP acceptance | E01 kernel/testing, generated contracts and composition; E23 inputs; requests below before affected integration |
| T2 | Warning screens, reconciliation, attention and real browser acceptance | T1; E03 shell, E20 client infrastructure and accepted projection/routing contracts |

T2 can prepare component tests and layouts against generated contracts while T1 implements the core. Its integration and completion wait for T1. The dependency records that real dependency, rather than allowing a mock hub to satisfy it. No two coders edit one file. SYSTEM.md sections 9 and 10 govern external dependencies and kernel fakes.

At inspection, `hub/`, `ui/`, `eval/`, `contracts/api/` and deployment warning configuration were absent; `config/` and `contracts/` contained the separate pharmacy engine. `fixtures/` contained pharmacy input only. E24 has no implementation to replace. `docs/requests/E24.md` was absent. Existing build allocations were checked, including E02, E03, E05 and E21 and the empty task lists present for E07, E08, E09 and E14. Other task lists were arriving during inspection, including E10; the final ownership check covers all currently present allocations. E29 design/request files were absent on the final recheck, so their previously observed declarations are not an integration prerequisite considered delivered. Recheck all allocations before dispatch because planners are working concurrently. E03 retains its shell, design components and `config/ui-copy.json`; E21 retains the runner, shared scenario setup and demo fixture. No task owns those paths or pharmacy files.

T1 implements only the exact section 13 Python files, its test tree, producer contract test and `config/warning-rules.json`. T2 owns only `ui/crew/src/features/warnings/`, including its tests, `routes.ts` and `slots.ts`. SYSTEM.md:1596 requires a registration file omitted from E24 section 13. Its ownership is a coordinator prerequisite, not permission to hide assembly side effects in an initializer.

## How the pieces connect

The real producer commits input and dispatches through SYSTEM.md section 5.7. E01's section 5.10.2 isolation invokes E24's versioned evaluator. E24 applies decisions through owned repositories; warning state, audit, outbox, declared replication changes and command receipts commit together. Queries apply current object/field grants and guidance eligibility. E03 consumes `WarningQueries`; E25 consumes `WarningRaised` and `WarningCleared`; E12/E13 use the guard and insight port. Consumers never read warning tables.

T2 reads the three warning operations and the existing Today/event APIs through the generated client. Lifecycle revisions and session projections reconcile separately. Shell slots mount attention on every surface. A missing optional model, device, forecast or ground process cannot stop rule warnings, manual input or fixed help. Missing required infrastructure blocks acceptance and remains visible.

## End to end proofs

All tests use the explicit `demo-mara-fd19` profile, normal `create_app(settings)` composition and real SQLite in a temporary data directory, or Playwright against that running composition. No mocked service, dependency override, direct SQL seed or intercepted HTTP response inside the tested stack counts. Kernel fakes are for unit/port tests. Only documented external worker/adapter fakes are permitted. HTTP journeys live under T1's `hub/tests/rules/`; browser journeys live under T2's feature directory. Moving them to `eval/` or `e2e/warnings` requires the ownership handoff requested below.

Every section 12.1 acceptance row and every section 12.2 test ID remains accounted for. R36/R40/R43 and warning evidence for R35/R39 are retained. T1 owns backend/unit/contract/fault/CPU/SQL measurements; T2 owns component/keyboard/multiscreen/latency/workload measurements. T1 also requires T2's browser evidence before whole-epic acceptance. T-E24-136 remains E25 authored; 137/138 require the real providers. Missing requests or providers fail completion; no skips, xfails, removed clauses or approval note substitutes for passing tests. The full E24 test directory and browser directory are selected without scenario filters.

## Design deviations

| Frozen section / review | Rule that wins | What to build |
|---|---|---|
| 3.5/3.8, 5.2; r2.8/9 | Part A D1, SYSTEM.md:536, DEPLOYMENT.md:638 | Retain original definition/limit/content/clear pins. Activation cannot clear, lower or switch an active warning to a new clearing rule. Current-release facts raise new warnings. Do not use environment activation as proof of recovery. Definition removal is permitted with retained pin and withdrawn indication once its representation is agreed; do not impose the design's blanket active-definition removal veto. Pinned clearing seam is R-E23-19. |
| 3.3/3.10/4.1; r2.13/14 | Part A D1, SYSTEM.md sections 8.3/8.4 | Manual rule/sensor resolution needs medical officer authorization, current object/action grant and reason. Self resolution is not automatically allowed by `person_may_resolve`; officer/acting status and `HelpSessionReader.readable_by` grant no general chart. R-E24-21 must be narrowed to this rule; no unapproved care exception. |
| 3.6/3.11/4.3; r2.4 | Part A D3/D14, SYSTEM.md sections 5.2/5.4 | Corrected observation time and its entire uncertainty interval determine LIVE/SIM freshness; evidence must follow the warning's raising time. REPLAY uses advancing-E receive reference for freshness and original data time for windows/dwell. Same raw time in different segments is distinct; unknown time cannot clear. Use `Quantity(value: Decimal, unit: Unit)`, not `unit: str`. Missing TimeInput and unit-bearing producer fields require agreement. |
| 3.12/7.2/8; r2.5/16 | Part A D2/Q9, SYSTEM.md:1964 | Storm is Emergency now, not awaiting clinical approval. During sleep Act routes immediately to an awake officer/on-duty crew member; only expiry without acknowledgement wakes the sleeper. E24 owns a generation-checked elapsed routing timer. Lower levels wait. EVA suppression remains. Missing routing DTO/configuration is a prerequisite, not permission to invent a time or disable the required cascade. |
| 2/4.1/4.2/5.1/5.5; r2.6 | Part A D13, SYSTEM.md:1443 and section 8.6 | E01 `EvaluationIsolation` alone owns savepoint/pending/retry/completion. Catch only `EvaluatorComputationFailure`; remove local pending table, coalescing, overflow replay, broad catch and quarantine-to-resume behavior. Adapt `pending.py` and CLI only to agreed shared APIs. Clears freeze on relevant shared pending state, including E23 failure before event construction. R-E23-18 supplies the missing transaction-bound read. |
| 3.16/10/12 T130/INV-19; r2.12 | Part A Q1/Q7/Q18, SYSTEM.md section 8.2 | Clinical review is a visible state, never a runtime gate. Preserve source/hash/purpose/pin/environment/origin checks. `warning_steps` is still absent from ContentRef: do not instantiate it or fake guidance success before accepted extension. Unknown source/purpose is unsupported; SIM is not a waiver. |

Use full operation/target/semantic-parameter/body identity, no durable flag. Reauthorize cached results. After cache expiry return the closed accepted-command receipt, never the Warning in `current_state`; private bodies are not cached. Replay precedes mutable checks. |

The remaining review corrections are retained, not reopened: r1.1 to r1.16 and r2.1 to r2.17 are tracked by the scenario rows and task tests. In particular keep per-definition/equal-level sensor hazards and per-limit rendering (r1.3, r2.10), durable outstanding occurrences (r1.4, r2.3), independent goldens and nonempty complete acceptance (r1.16, r2.12/17). Response documents' unconditional fixed labels are not proof of approved requests or runtime correctness. Both cold reviews still say CHANGES REQUESTED.

## Verification

Planner checks validated JSON shape, dependency order, current source reads, section 13 ownership, disjoint allocations and writing constraints. The frozen-design command `.venv/bin/python -B scripts/design_lint.py docs/tdd/E24.md --json` returned 1 with 133 errors and 27 warnings. Findings include absent request filings, missing template/rule-trace sections, seam/schema recognition and acceptance-marker recognition. Coordinator: settle the actual missing declarations and have the gate owner resolve recognition defects with evidence; neither edits to the frozen design nor a waiver are authorized here. Product and CI gates were not run because their implementation/toolchain is absent.
